s1.syndrome_frame: Multi-system inflammatory syndrome with fever, rash, abdominal symptoms, and cardiovascular involvement
salient_findings: Macular rash on chest and arms
Bilaterally coarse crepitations on lung exam
Elevated liver enzymes and cardiac markers
key_facts: 18-year-old African male with no prior medical history
2-day history of tonsillitis
New macular rash on chest and arms
Abdominal cramping and multiple episodes of non-bloody diarrhea
Fever and joint pains in wrists, elbows, and knees
Initial outpatient care included oral chlorhexidine, lozenges, and symptomatic treatment
High fever, tachycardia, and confusion
Rising serum creatinine from 200 to 400 μmol/L
Received ceftriaxone, paracetamol, loperamide, and one dose of IV methylprednisolone
Febrile, hypotensive, tachycardic, tachypneic, and hypoxemic on arrival
GCS was 14/15
Lung exam revealed bilaterally coarse crepitations
Cardiovascular exam revealed audible S3 gallop
Abdomen distended and tense with hypoactive bowel sounds
WBC 27.1×10^9/L, Hb 10.9 g/dL, platelets 281×10^9/L
Procalcitonin 71.6 ng/mL, CRP 287 mg/L
Creatinine 494 μmol/L, urea 26.7 mmol/L
Liver tests showed AST 1461 U/L and ALT 812 U/L
Hepatitis A, B, C, and HIV screens were negative
Urinalysis had 3+ protein and 4+ blood without RBCs
Urine albumin:creatinine ratio was 52.3 mg/mmol
Cardiac markers were elevated (troponin 17 137 ng/mL; CK > 7800 U/L)

shortlist.label: Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with fever, rash, and hypotension, which are consistent with streptococcal toxic shock syndrome

shortlist.label: Kawasaki disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms, including fever, rash, and cardiovascular involvement, are consistent with Kawasaki disease

shortlist.label: Meningococcemia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with fever, rash, and hypotension, which are consistent with meningococcemia

shortlist.label: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms, including fever, rash, and elevated liver enzymes, are consistent with hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis

shortlist.label: Macrophage activation syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms, including fever, rash, and elevated liver enzymes, are consistent with macrophage activation syndrome

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with high fever, tachycardia, hypotension, and multi-organ involvement (renal failure, liver dysfunction, and cardiac markers elevation) is consistent with streptococcal toxic shock syndrome. The initial symptoms of tonsillitis and rash also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Kawasaki disease
rejected.why: The patient's age and lack of typical Kawasaki disease features such as conjunctivitis and lymphadenopathy make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Meningococcemia
rejected.why: The absence of a petechial rash and the patient's initial presentation with tonsillitis and abdominal symptoms do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated liver enzymes and coagulopathy, the primary presentation and progression of the illness do not strongly suggest hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis

rejected.label: Macrophage activation syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's clinical presentation and laboratory findings, such as the absence of significant lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly, do not support this diagnosis
